I. रुचि की अभिव्यक्ति (Expression of Interest - EoI) के लिए आमंत्रण
II. कार्य संदर्भ (Terms of Reference - ToR) तैयार करना
III. सलाहकारों की संक्षिप्त सूची (शॉर्टलिस्टिंग) तैयार करना
IV. तकनीकी और वित्तीय बोलियों का मूल्यांकन करना

questions.question_english:
Arrange the following steps for the procurement of consulting services in the correct order:
I. Invitation for Expression of Interest (EoI)
II. Preparation of Terms of Reference (ToR)
III. Shortlisting of consultants
IV. Evaluation of Technical and Financial bids
questions.explanation_english:
Under Chapter 6 (Procurement of Services) of GFR 2017, the sequential stages for procuring consulting services follow a prescribed legal hierarchy:
1. Step II: Preparation of Terms of Reference (ToR) (Rule 185) - Formulating the foundational document specifying the project background, objectives, scope of work, and expected deliverables.
2. Step I: Invitation for Expression of Interest (EoI) (Rule 186) - Publishing an open notice (mandatory for estimated costs exceeding Rs. 25 Lakhs) to invite expressions of interest from competent consulting firms.
3. Step III: Shortlisting of Consultants (Rule 187) - Evaluating EoI submissions against pre-announced criteria and shortlisting a manageable number of qualified firms (normally 3 to 8).
4. Step IV: Issue of Request for Proposals (RFP) & Evaluation of Technical and Financial Bids (Rules 188 to 193) - Inviting detailed proposals from shortlisted firms, conducting two-stage bid evaluations, and selecting the successful consultant.
Therefore, the correct chronological order is II -> I -> III -> IV.
questions.explanation_hindi:
GFR 2017 के अध्याय 6 (सेवाओं की खरीद) के अनुसार परामर्श सेवाओं की खरीद के चरणों का सही वैधानिक क्रम इस प्रकार है:
1. चरण II: कार्य संदर्भ (Terms of Reference - ToR) तैयार करना (नियम 185) - यह आधारभूत दस्तावेज है जिसमें परियोजना के उद्देश्य, कार्य का दायरा और डिलिवरेबल्स निर्धारित किए जाते हैं।
2. चरण I: रुचि की अभिव्यक्ति (EoI) का आमंत्रण (नियम 186) - योग्य सलाहकार फर्मों से आवेदन आमंत्रित करने के लिए सार्वजनिक विज्ञापन जारी करना।
3. चरण III: सलाहकारों की संक्षिप्त सूची (शॉर्टलिस्टिंग) बनाना (नियम 187) - प्राप्त आवेदनों की पात्रता का मूल्यांकन करके योग्य फर्मों की एक संक्षिप्त सूची तैयार करना।
4. चरण IV: तकनीकी और वित्तीय बोलियों का मूल्यांकन करना (नियम 188 से 193) - शॉर्टलिस्टेड फर्मों से प्रस्ताव मांगकर तकनीकी और वित्तीय बोलियों का मूल्यांकन करना तथा अनुबंध प्रदान करना।
अतः सही क्रम II -> I -> III -> IV है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) II, I, III, IV

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Procuring consulting services follows a structured sequence. The process begins with preparing detailed Terms of Reference defining objectives and deliverables. Next, the department issues an invitation for Expression of Interest to identify potential candidates. The authority then shortlists qualified firms, followed by receiving, evaluating, and scoring technical and financial proposals to select the winner.

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The release of subsequent installments of Grants-in-aid to an institution is generally conditional upon the submission and acceptance of the Utilization Certificate (UC) for the previous installment.
Reason (R): This statutory requirement ensures that previously sanctioned public funds have been genuinely utilized on the authorized objectives before committing further exchequer resources.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 238(1) of GFR 2017, no further grant or subsequent installment shall be released to any institution or organization unless the Utilization Certificate in respect of the previous grant/installment has been submitted to the satisfaction of the sanctioning administrative ministry or department. The core rationale of this financial rule is to maintain rigorous financial discipline, prevent parking of public funds in bank accounts, eliminate unspent surplus accumulation, and guarantee that previous public moneys have been legitimately spent on the intended objectives before committing additional government resources. Thus, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are both true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation_hindi: जीएफआर (GFR), 2017 के नियम 238(1) के अनुसार, किसी भी संस्थान या संगठन को सहायता अनुदान की अगली किस्त या नया अनुदान तब तक जारी नहीं किया जाएगा जब तक कि पिछली किस्त का उपयोग प्रमाण पत्र (UC) संतोषजनक रूप से प्रस्तुत न कर दिया गया हो। इस वित्तीय नियम का मुख्य उद्देश्य वित्तीय अनुशासन बनाए रखना, अनुदान प्राप्तकर्ता के खातों में सरकारी धन के अप्रयुक्त जमा (parking of funds) को रोकना तथा यह पुख्ता करना है कि अतिरिक्त सार्वजनिक संसाधन जारी करने से पहले पूर्व में आवंटित धनराशि का निर्धारित उद्देश्य हेतु वैध उपयोग हो चुका है। अतः अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं और (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: correct explanation of (A) Releasing subsequent grant installments to an institution is generally contingent upon receiving a satisfactory Utilization Certificate for previous funds. This regulatory check ensures that prior allocations were properly expended on approved objectives before committing additional public funds, thereby maintaining financial control and preventing unspent balances from accumulating in grantee accounts.

I. इसमें कार्यालय के प्रबंधन के लिए आवश्यक सभी प्रासंगिक (incidental) और अन्य व्यय शामिल हैं।

III. इसमें भंडारों (stores) पर होने वाला व्यय शामिल नहीं होता है।
IV. इसमें कार्यालय फर्नीचर की खरीद और छोटी-मोटी मरम्मत पर होने वाला व्यय शामिल है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding "Contingent Expenditure" as defined under the General Financial Rules (GFR):
I. It includes all incidental and operational expenses necessary for the routine management of an office.
II. It encompasses regular monthly salary and allowance disbursements to permanent staff.
III. It strictly excludes expenditure incurred on all types of stores.
IV. It includes expenditure incurred on purchasing office furniture and carrying out minor repairs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation_english: Under GFR and Government accounting rules, 'Contingent Expenditure' (or Contingencies) means that class of expenditure which comprises incidental and other expenses incurred on the management of an office (e.g., stationery, postage, minor repairs, office furniture within delegated limits, electricity/water bills, freight). It explicitly excludes establishment charges (salaries, allowances, and honoraria of regular government servants). Minor store purchases necessary for office maintenance fall within contingencies. Hence, Statement I is correct, Statement II is incorrect, Statement III is incorrect (office stores/stationery are part of contingencies), and Statement IV is correct. Thus, I and IV are the correct statements.
questions.explanation_hindi: GFR और सरकारी लेखा नियमों के अनुसार, 'आकस्मिक व्यय' (Contingent Expenditure) से तात्पर्य कार्यालय के दैनिक संचालन और प्रबंधन के लिए आवश्यक प्रासंगिक खर्चों से है। इसमें डाक टिकट, स्टेशनरी, बिजली-पानी के बिल, छोटी मरम्मतें और निर्धारित सीमा के भीतर कार्यालय फर्नीचर आदि शामिल होते हैं (कथन I और IV सही हैं)। आकस्मिक व्यय में नियमित कर्मचारियों के वेतन और भत्ते (Establishment Charges) शामिल नहीं होते (कथन II गलत है)। कार्यालय संचालन हेतु आवश्यक छोटे भंडार (stores) आकस्मिक व्यय का ही भाग होते हैं, अतः कथन III भी गलत है। इसलिए सही उत्तर 'केवल I और IV' है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) I and IV

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Contingent expenditure comprises all incidental administrative expenses necessary for the routine operational management and functioning of a government establishment. It includes costs incurred for office stationery, minor structural repairs, utility payments, and office furniture procurement. However, regular establishment charges like fixed salaries, permanent staff allowances, and major public store acquisitions are strictly excluded from the scope of contingent expenditure.

अभिकथन (A): कोई प्रशासनिक प्राधिकारी अपने अधीनस्थ अधिकारी को अपनी वित्तीय शक्तियां तब तक उप-प्रत्यायोजित (sub-delegate) नहीं कर सकता, जब तक कि विधिक नियमों या सक्षम प्राधिकारी के आदेश द्वारा ऐसा करने के लिए स्पष्ट रूप से अधिकृत न किया गया हो।
कारण (R): उप-प्रत्यायोजन से वित्तीय उत्तरदायित्व क्षीण (dilute) होता है, और मूल प्रत्यायोजन प्राधिकारी को राजकोषीय जिम्मेदारी की एक अटूट श्रृंखला बनाए रखना आवश्यक होता है।

(A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं लेकिन (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): An administrative authority cannot sub-delegate its financial powers to a subordinate officer unless expressly authorized to do so by statutory rules or an order of the competent authority.
Reason (R): Sub-delegation dilutes financial accountability, and the original delegating authority must maintain an unbroken chain of fiscal responsibility.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation_english:
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
- Assertion (A) is correct: Under administrative law and the Delegation of Financial Powers Rules (DFPR), the legal maxim 'delegatus non potest delegare' (a delegate cannot further delegate) strictly applies to financial sanctions. A Head of Department or Head of Office cannot redelegate financial powers to subordinate officials without explicit statutory backing or sanction from the Ministry of Finance / Competent Authority.
- Reason (R) is correct and explains (A): The constitutional and statutory purpose of restricting sub-delegation is to preserve a clear, unbroken line of accountability. If financial powers could be casually passed down, accountability for financial propriety and budgetary control would become diffused, leading to fiscal indiscipline and audit lapses. Hence, (R) provides the direct institutional rationale for (A).
questions.explanation_hindi:
अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
- अभिकथन (A) सही है: प्रशासनिक विधि और DFPR के तहत 'प्रत्यायोजित प्राधिकारी आगे प्रत्यायोजन नहीं कर सकता' (delegatus non potest delegare) का सिद्धांत सख्ती से लागू होता है। वित्तीय शक्तियां प्राप्त कोई अधिकारी सक्षम प्राधिकारी या नियमों के स्पष्ट आदेश के बिना अपनी वित्तीय शक्तियां निचले अधिकारियों को नहीं सौंप सकता।
- कारण (R) सही है और (A) की सटीक व्याख्या करता है: उप-प्रत्यायोजन पर प्रतिबंध लगाने का मूल उद्देश्य वित्तीय उत्तरदायित्व की स्पष्ट श्रृंखला बनाए रखना है। यदि शक्तियों को स्वेच्छा से नीचे हस्तांतरित करने की अनुमति दी जाए, तो सार्वजनिक धन के उपयोग की जवाबदेही धुंधली हो जाएगी और वित्तीय अनियमितताओं की संभावना बढ़ जाएगी। अतः (R), (A) का सही कारण है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: correct explanation of (A) Financial authority cannot be sub-delegated to lower officers unless explicit regulatory provisions or formal orders permit such transfer. Restricting sub-delegation ensures clear lines of administrative responsibility, prevents dilution of financial accountability, and guarantees that expenditure sanctions remain strictly within authorized supervisory controls across government establishments.

questions.question_english: Under GFR 2017 and the Compendium of Rules on Advances, advances to government servants are regulated by specific guidelines. Which of the following is classified as an interest-bearing advance?
questions.explanation_english:
Under the General Financial Rules (GFR) and the Compendium of Rules on Advances to Government Servants, advances are broadly categorized into two classes:
1. Interest-bearing advances: Advances granted for specific capital assets or welfare purposes where the employee is required to repay the principal amount along with interest calculated at rates prescribed by the Ministry of Finance from time to time. Personal Computer Advance (PCA) and House Building Advance (HBA) are classic examples of interest-bearing advances retained after the 7th Central Pay Commission (7th CPC).
2. Non-interest-bearing advances: Advances granted to facilitate the discharge of official duties or contingent travel requirements. These include Travelling Allowance (TA) advance on tour or transfer, advance of pay on transfer, and Leave Travel Concession (LTC) advance. These carry no interest provided they are adjusted or refunded within the prescribed statutory time limits.
Therefore, Computer Advance is an interest-bearing advance.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR) और सरकारी कर्मचारियों को अग्रिम नियमों के संग्रह के अनुसार, सरकारी सेवकों को दिए जाने वाले अग्रिमों को मुख्य रूप से दो श्रेणियों में विभाजित किया गया है:
1. ब्याज सहित अग्रिम (Interest-bearing advances): वे अग्रिम जो विशिष्ट पूंजीगत परिसंपत्तियों या कल्याणकारी उद्देश्यों हेतु दिए जाते हैं, जिनमें कर्मचारी को मूलधन के साथ-साथ वित्त मंत्रालय द्वारा समय-समय पर निर्धारित ब्याज दर का भी भुगतान करना होता है। 7वें केंद्रीय वेतन आयोग (7th CPC) के बाद बरकरार रखे गए 'कंप्यूटर अग्रिम' (Personal Computer Advance) और 'भवन निर्माण अग्रिम' (HBA) इसके प्रमुख उदाहरण हैं।
2. ब्याज मुक्त अग्रिम (Non-interest-bearing advances): सरकारी कर्तव्यों के निष्पादन अथवा यात्रा संबंधी आकस्मिक व्यय हेतु दिए जाने वाले अग्रिम ब्याज मुक्त होते हैं। जैसे- आधिकारिक दौरे या स्थानांतरण पर यात्रा भत्ता (TA) अग्रिम, स्थानांतरण पर वेतन अग्रिम, तथा अवकाश यात्रा रियायत (LTC) अग्रिम। निर्धारित समय-सीमा के भीतर इनका समायोजन या वापसी करने पर कोई ब्याज नहीं लिया जाता है।
अतः, कंप्यूटर अग्रिम एक ब्याज सहित अग्रिम है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Computer Advance

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Advances granted to government employees fall into interest-bearing and non-interest-bearing categories. Computer advance is classified as an interest-bearing advance, requiring repayment of principal followed by interest accrued at government-prescribed interest rates. Conversely, duty-related advances such as travel allowances for official tours, transfer advances, and leave travel concessions are non-interest-bearing personal advances.

questions.question_english: Which rule in the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017 defines the "Fundamental principles of public buying"?
questions.explanation_english:
Rule 144 of Chapter 6 of GFR 2017 explicitly defines the "Fundamental principles of public buying".

Scope of Rule 144:
1. Core Yardsticks: It establishes the yardsticks governing every public procurement, requiring procuring authorities to bring efficiency, economy, and transparency, ensure fair and equitable treatment of suppliers, and promote open competition.
2. Distinct from other rules:
   - Rule 21: Standards of Financial Propriety.
   - Rule 130: Execution of original works and repair works.
   - Rule 144: Fundamental principles of public buying (Procurement of Goods).
   - Rule 170: Bid Security (Earnest Money Deposit - EMD).
questions.explanation_hindi:
GFR 2017 के अध्याय 6 का नियम 144 स्पष्ट रूप से "सार्वजनिक खरीद के मौलिक सिद्धांत" (Fundamental principles of public buying) को परिभाषित करता है।

नियम 144 का दायरा:
1. मुख्य मानक: यह प्रत्येक सार्वजनिक खरीद को नियंत्रित करने वाले मानकों को स्थापित करता है, जिसके तहत खरीद प्राधिकारियों को दक्षता, मितव्ययिता और पारदर्शिता सुनिश्चित करनी होती है, आपूर्तिकर्ताओं के साथ निष्पक्ष व्यवहार करना होता है और खुली प्रतिस्पर्धा को बढ़ावा देना होता है।
2. अन्य नियमों से भिन्नता:
   - नियम 21: वित्तीय औचित्य के मानक।
   - नियम 130: मूल निर्माण कार्यों और मरम्मत कार्यों का निष्पादन।
   - नियम 144: सार्वजनिक खरीद के मौलिक सिद्धांत (वस्तुओं की खरीद)।
   - नियम 170: बोली सुरक्षा (बयाना राशि - EMD)।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Rule 144

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Rule 144 of the General Financial Rules 2017 establishes the fundamental principles governing public buying and procurement of goods. This rule outlines essential yardsticks that every procuring authority must follow, mandating efficiency, economy, fairness, equal treatment of suppliers, transparency, and accountability in all procurement operations to ensure that public money achieves optimum value without administrative bias or procedural delays.

questions.question_english: The Principal of a Government Boys Senior Secondary School is designated as the Head of Office. A teacher submits a bill for the purchase of classroom teaching aids. Prior to forwarding the bill to the Pay and Accounts Office (PAO) for payment, what is the most appropriate action the Principal must take under GFR rules and DDO responsibilities?
options_english: Verify that expenditure sanction was accorded by the competent authority, confirm physical receipt of items in good condition, and verify entries in the official stock register.
Forward the bill immediately to the Pay and Accounts Office without verifying stock register entries to avoid payment delay.
Direct the teacher to defray the cost from personal funds and seek reimbursement at the close of the financial year.
Forward the bill directly to the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, for prior clearance.
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 12, Rule 144, and Rule 207-211 (Procurement and Inventory Management) of GFR 2017, as well as DDO rules, before passing any bill or forwarding it to the Pay and Accounts Office (PAO), the Head of Office / DDO must satisfy themselves that: (i) the expenditure has been sanctioned by the Competent Authority within delegated financial limits; (ii) the items purchased have been physically received in full count and satisfactory working condition; (iii) the non-consumable/consumable articles have been duly entered in the appropriate school Stock Register with the relevant page number and certificate recorded on the invoice bill; and (iv) the rates and arithmetical calculations are correct. Bypassing stock verification is a serious financial irregularity.
questions.explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 (नियम 12, 144 एवं नियम 207-211 भंडार और माल सूची प्रबंधन) तथा DDO नियमावली के अनुसार, वेतन एवं लेखा कार्यालय (PAO) को बिल भेजने से पूर्व कार्यालय प्रमुख (प्रधानाचार्य) को अनिवार्य रूप से यह सत्यापित करना होता है कि: 1. खरीद हेतु सक्षम प्राधिकारी से प्रशासनिक व वित्तीय स्वीकृति प्राप्त है; 2. सामान सही मात्रा और गुणवत्ता में प्राप्त हो चुका है; 3. सामान की प्रविष्टि स्कूल के स्टॉक रजिस्टर (उपभोज्य/अनुपभोज्य) में विधिवत कर दी गई है और बिल पर स्टॉक एंट्री का प्रमाण पत्र व पृष्ठ संख्या अंकित कर दी गई है; तथा 4. दरें व गणनाएं सही हैं। स्टॉक सत्यापन के बिना बिल पास करना वित्तीय नियमों का गंभीर उल्लंघन है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Verify sanction by competent authority and receipt of items in good condition.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: receipt of items in good condition. Before presenting any financial claim to the accounts office, an administrative head acting as the head of office must rigorously verify the underlying documentation. This includes verifying that the purchase received proper administrative sanction from a competent authority, verifying that goods were delivered in satisfactory physical condition, and ensuring that all items were recorded in the official stock register appropriately.

questions.question_hindi: एक विद्यालय के प्राचार्य ने विद्यालय के कमर्शियल आरओ (RO) वाटर प्यूरीफायर प्रणालियों के लिए एक निश्चित दर पर वार्षिक रखरखाव अनुबंध (AMC) निष्पादित किया। अनुबंध की अवधि के मध्य में, विक्रेता सामान्य मुद्रास्फीति का हवाला देते हुए रखरखाव दर को दोगुना करने का अनुरोध करता है, जबकि अनुबंध में कोई मूल्य भिन्नता खंड (Price Variation Clause) शामिल नहीं है। एक आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) / कार्यालय प्रमुख के रूप में प्राचार्य को क्या कदम उठाना चाहिए?

questions.question_english: A school Principal enters into a firm fixed-price Annual Maintenance Contract (AMC) for the school's commercial RO water purification systems. Mid-way through the contract tenure, the vendor requests doubling the maintenance charges citing general inflation, even though the contract contains no price variation clause. As a responsible Head of Office / DDO, what action should the Principal take under GFR rules?
options_english: Approve the enhanced maintenance rates immediately to ensure uninterrupted supply of potable water for students.
Reject the request firmly, as terms of an executed contract cannot be modified to the detriment of the Government without explicit contractual provisions.
Terminate the agreement unilaterally and pay liquidated damages and penalty to the vendor from Vidyalaya Kalyan Samiti (VKS) funds.
Direct the School Management Committee (SMC) to levy and collect extra maintenance fees from students to cover the contractor's increased rates.
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 225(vi) and (viii) of GFR 2017, contract terms must be precise, definite, and strictly adhered to. Once a public contract is executed on a firm fixed-price basis without an explicit Price Variation Clause (PVC), no relaxation or variation of terms involving financial concessions or higher expenditure to the detriment of the Government can be granted. A contractor is legally bound to fulfill the contractual scope at the agreed rates throughout the contract validity. Any mid-term revision requested by the vendor due to market fluctuations or inflation cannot be entertained by the Principal/DDO, as doing so would violate contract sanctity and the canons of financial propriety. Thus, the Principal must reject the vendor's request.
questions.explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 के नियम 225(vi) और (viii) के अनुसार, सरकारी अनुबंध की शर्तें स्पष्ट, निश्चित और बाध्यकारी होनी चाहिए। एक बार जब कोई सार्वजनिक अनुबंध बिना मूल्य भिन्नता खंड (Price Variation Clause) के निश्चित दर पर निष्पादित कर दिया जाता है, तो अनुबंध की अवधि के दौरान सरकार के वित्तीय अहित में या ठेकेदार को वित्तीय रियायत देने वाला कोई भी संशोधन नहीं किया जा सकता। ठेकेदार सहमत दरों पर ही पूरी अनुबंध अवधि तक सेवाएं प्रदान करने के लिए विधिक रूप से बाध्य है। मुद्रास्फीति या बाजार में उतार-चढ़ाव का हवाला देकर दरों में बढ़ोतरी के विक्रेता के अनुरोध को स्वीकार करना वित्तीय औचित्य के सिद्धांतों और संविदात्मक पवित्रता का उल्लंघन होगा। इसलिए प्राचार्य को इस अनुरोध को सिरे से खारिज करना चाहिए। अतः विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Reject request as contract terms should not be varied to Government detriment without specific provision.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: be varied to Government detriment without specific provision. Public contract terms cannot be varied after execution to the financial detriment of the government unless specific contractual clauses or explicit legal conditions permit adjustment. A contractor's mid-term request to increase agreed maintenance rates without a price variation clause must be rejected to uphold contract sanctity and financial propriety.

questions.question_english: While Internal Audit is conducted departmentally by the Internal Audit Wing of the respective Ministry or Department, who holds the constitutional mandate to conduct the final External (Statutory) Audit of Government accounts in India?
options_english: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) acting through its Chief Vigilance Officers
Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) Economic Offences Wing
Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India
Department of Expenditure in the Ministry of Finance
questions.explanation_english: Under Articles 148 to 151 of the Constitution of India and the Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 (CAG's DPC Act), the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is an independent supreme constitutional authority vested with the exclusive mandate to conduct the external, statutory audit of all receipts and expenditures of the Union and State governments, as well as bodies substantially financed by government funds. While departmental internal audit is an executive tool reporting to the Secretary/Head of Department, statutory audit reports prepared by the CAG are placed directly before Parliament or state legislatures and are examined in detail by parliamentary financial committees such as the Public Accounts Committee (PAC).
questions.explanation_hindi: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 148 से 151 तथा नियंत्रक एवं महालेखापरीक्षक (कर्तव्य, शक्तियां एवं सेवा शर्तें) अधिनियम, 1971 (CAG's DPC Act) के तहत भारत के नियंत्रक एवं महालेखापरीक्षक (CAG) को केंद्र और राज्य सरकारों के सभी प्राप्तियों एवं व्ययों की अंतिम बाह्य (सांविधिक) लेखापरीक्षा करने का अनन्य संवैधानिक अधिकार प्राप्त है। आंतरिक लेखापरीक्षा जहां कार्यपालिका का आंतरिक नियंत्रण साधन है और विभाग के प्रशासनिक सचिव को रिपोर्ट करती है, वहीं कैग की सांविधिक लेखापरीक्षा स्वतंत्र रूप से आयोजित की जाती है और इसकी रिपोर्ट सीधे संसद अथवा राज्य विधानमंडलों के समक्ष रखी जाती है, जिसकी समीक्षा लोक लेखा समिति (PAC) द्वारा की जाती है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (c) Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: India While internal audit is conducted by departmental accounting wings, the constitutional mandate for conducting final external statutory audits of government accounts rests exclusively with the Comptroller and Auditor General of India. The CAG independently audits public revenues and expenditures, submitting statutory audit reports directly to Parliament and state legislatures.

questions.question_english: What does the term "Delegation of Financial Powers" refer to in the context of the Delegation of Financial Powers Rules (DFPR) and GFR?
options_english: Centralizing all financial decision-making authority exclusively at the level of the Prime Minister's Office.
The legal devolution and transfer of financial decision-making and sanctioning authority to subordinate authorities to facilitate prompt administration.
The formal administrative process of surrendering unspent budget allocations to the Ministry of Finance.
Transferring surplus government revenue funds into private commercial banks to earn higher interest rates.
questions.explanation_english: Under the Delegation of Financial Powers Rules (DFPR), 1978 and Rule 22 of GFR 2017, the "Delegation of Financial Powers" refers to the statutory process by which the President of India (or the Ministry of Finance) delegates specific financial sanctioning authorities to administrative Ministries, Heads of Departments (HoD), and Heads of Offices (HoO) / Drawing and Disbursing Officers (DDOs), such as school Principals. The objective is to decentralize operational decision-making, prevent administrative bottlenecks, and empower field officers to execute sanctioned schemes, contingent expenditures, and procurements efficiently within prescribed monetary limits and budgetary allocations, while holding them accountable for compliance with financial rules.
questions.explanation_hindi: वित्तीय शक्ति प्रत्यायोजन नियमावली (DFPR), 1978 तथा जीएफआर 2017 के नियम 22 के तहत, "वित्तीय शक्तियों का प्रत्यायोजन" उस विधिक प्रक्रिया को संदर्भित करता है जिसके द्वारा राष्ट्रपति अथवा वित्त मंत्रालय प्रशासनिक मंत्रालयों, विभागाध्यक्षों (HoD) तथा कार्यालयाध्यक्षों (HoO) / आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारियों (DDO) जैसे कि विद्यालय प्राचार्यों को विशिष्ट वित्तीय स्वीकृति अधिकार सौंपते हैं। इसका प्राथमिक उद्देश्य निर्णय प्रक्रिया का विकेंद्रीकरण करना, प्रशासनिक विलंब को दूर करना और क्षेत्रीय अधिकारियों को निर्धारित मौद्रिक सीमाओं और बजट आवंटन के भीतर आकस्मिक व्यय, खरीद और योजनाओं के कार्यान्वयन के लिए अधिकृत करना है, साथ ही वित्तीय उत्तरदायित्व भी सुनिश्चित करना है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) The legal transfer of financial decision- making authority to subordinate authorities to facilitate administration.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: making authority to subordinate authorities to facilitate administration. Delegation of financial powers involves the administrative transfer of financial sanctioning authority from central authorities to subordinate administrative officers. This delegation decentralizes decision-making, expedites routine administrative workflows, prevents operational bottlenecks, and improves administrative efficiency while enforcing financial accountability within established monetary thresholds and statutory regulatory guidelines.

questions.question_english: According to the operational provisions of Rule 149 of GFR 2017, up to what financial ceiling can a government buyer make a direct online purchase on GeM from any available seller meeting the required quality, specification, and delivery period?
questions.explanation_english:
Rule 149 of GFR 2017 prescribes the financial thresholds for procurement on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM):
1. Up to Rs. 25,000/-: Direct online purchase can be made from any available seller on GeM who meets the requisite quality, specification, and delivery period (without mandatory comparison of multiple sellers).
2. Above Rs. 25,000/- and up to Rs. 5,00,000/-: Purchase is to be made through the seller offering the lowest price (L1) after comparing at least three different manufacturers/sellers on GeM meeting identical specifications.
3. Above Rs. 5,00,000/-: Mandatory procurement through online bidding or reverse auction tool provided on GeM.
Therefore, the direct purchase limit from any single seller meeting requirements without comparison under Rule 149(i) is up to Rs. 25,000/-.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the general principles of financial propriety under GFR 2017:

I. Expenditure should not be incurred for the benefit of a particular person or a section of the people unless a claim for the amount could be enforced in a Court of Law.
II. Expenditure for a particular person or section of the people is permissible if it is incurred in pursuance of a recognized public policy or custom.
III. Compensatory allowances may be regulated in a manner that serves as an alternative source of profit or income for employees.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation_english:
Statements I and II are correct, while Statement III is incorrect.

Statutory Provisions under Rule 21(iii) of GFR 2017:
1. Expenditure for Individuals/Sections: The rule lays down that expenditure from public moneys should not be incurred for the benefit of a particular person or a section of the people, unless:
   - (a) a claim for the amount could be enforced in a Court of Law (Statement I); or
   - (b) the expenditure is in pursuance of a recognized policy or custom (Statement II).
2. Regulation of Allowances: Rule 21(iii) also provides that allowances granted to meet expenditure should be so regulated that they are "not on the whole a source of profit to the recipient". Therefore, Statement III is diametrically opposed to the rule.
questions.explanation_hindi:
कथन I और II सही हैं, जबकि कथन III गलत है।

GFR 2017 के नियम 21(iii) के अंतर्गत वैधानिक प्रावधान:
1. विशिष्ट व्यक्तियों/वर्गों हेतु व्यय: नियम निर्धारित करता है कि सार्वजनिक धन से किसी विशेष व्यक्ति या जनसमूह के लाभ के लिए व्यय तब तक नहीं किया जाना चाहिए, जब तक कि:
   - (क) इस राशि का दावा किसी न्यायालय में कानूनी रूप से प्रवर्तित न कराया जा सके (कथन I); अथवा
   - (ख) यह व्यय किसी मान्यता प्राप्त नीति या प्रथा के अनुसरण में न हो (कथन II)।
2. भत्तों का विनियमन: नियम 21(iii) यह भी निर्देश देता है कि किसी विशेष व्यय की पूर्ति हेतु दिए जाने वाले भत्तों को इस प्रकार विनियमित किया जाए कि वे प्राप्तकर्ता के लिए "लाभ का स्रोत न बनें"। इसलिए, कथन III नियम के सर्वथा विपरीत है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I and II

Propriety rules demand strictly policy-oriented and legally backed financial allocations.

questions.explanation_english: Rule 211 of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017 sets out the classification of stores and government assets for maintaining accounts and registers. Under Rule 211(1), every storekeeper or officer custodian is required to maintain distinct accounts and stock registers for: (i) Fixed Assets (such as plant, machinery, equipment, furniture, fixtures, land, and buildings in Form GFR-22); (ii) Consumables (items consumed, exhausted, or transformed during routine office operations like stationery, chemicals, fuel, and cleaning materials in Form GFR-23); and (iii) Non-consumables (durable items that do not qualify as permanent infrastructure but retain physical identity over time and are recorded in Form GFR-22/durable stores register). This tri-fold classification ensures accurate inventory valuation, proper physical verification, and systematic depreciation or write-off accounting in government establishments and schools.

questions.question_english: Under the Supplementary Rules and central accounting guidelines, what is the stipulated time limit for a government employee to submit the adjustment bill for a TA advance taken for an official tour, following the completion of the return journey?

Under Supplementary Rules (SR) and the Compendium of Rules on Advances:
1. Prescribed Time Limit: A government employee who draws a travel allowance advance for an official tour is statutorily required to submit the final adjustment travel claim within 15 days of completing the return journey.

Consider the following statements regarding an Advertised Tender Enquiry (Open Tender) under Rule 161 of GFR 2017:
I. It should be adopted for the procurement of goods of estimated value of Rs. 25 lakhs and above.
II. The tender advertisement must mandatorily be published on the Central Public Procurement Portal (CPPP).

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 161 of GFR 2017:
1. Statement I is correct: Advertised Tender Enquiry (Open Competitive Bidding) is the standard method for procurement of goods of estimated value of Rs. 25 Lakhs and above.
2. Statement II is correct: Publication of tender notices on the Central Public Procurement Portal (CPPP) at www.eprocure.gov.in and on the ministry/department's website is mandatory. It is also published on GeM.
3. Statement III is incorrect: The minimum time allowed for submission of bids should ordinarily be three weeks (21 days) from the date of publication of the tender notice or availability of bidding documents for domestic tenders, and four weeks for international tenders. A window of only three days is completely inadequate and contrary to GFR rules.
Hence, only statements I and II are correct.

III. परिसंपत्ति रजिस्टर में लागत, अधिग्रहण की तिथि और भौतिक अवस्थिति (लोकेशन) जैसे विवरण आवश्यक होते हैं।
IV. अचल परिसंपत्तियों के किसी भी भौतिक सत्यापन की आवश्यकता नहीं होती है।

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the maintenance of an Asset Register under GFR 2017:
I. A Register of Fixed Assets must be maintained in the prescribed Form GFR-22.
II. Land, buildings, plant, and machinery are classified as fixed assets.
III. The asset register requires comprehensive details including cost, date of acquisition, and physical location.
IV. Fixed assets do not require any periodic physical verification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation_english:
Under GFR 2017:
- Statement I is correct: Rule 211(1)(i) explicitly mandates that the Register of Fixed Assets must be maintained in Form GFR-22.
- Statement II is correct: Fixed assets include permanent, immovable, and durable capital equipment such as land, buildings, plant, machinery, office vehicles, and standard apparatus.
- Statement III is correct: Form GFR-22 contains specific columns for entering the item description, serial number, historical purchase cost, date of acquisition, voucher reference, physical location/department, and disposal details.
- Statement IV is incorrect: Rule 213(1) of GFR 2017 explicitly states that physical verification of fixed assets must be conducted at least once in a year by a designated officer or committee to verify their physical existence, check working condition, and reconcile register balances with ground reality.
Therefore, statements I, II, and III are correct, making (A) the right option.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के तहत:
- कथन I सही है: नियम 211(1)(i) के अनुसार अचल परिसंपत्तियों का रजिस्टर फॉर्म GFR-22 में अनिवार्य रूप से रखा जाता है।
- कथन II सही है: भूमि, भवन, संयंत्र, मशीनरी, फर्नीचर और उपकरण अचल परिसंपत्तियों (Fixed Assets) के अंतर्गत आते हैं।
- कथन III सही है: फॉर्म GFR-22 में परिसंपत्ति का विवरण, अधिग्रहण की तिथि, खरीद मूल्य/लागत, वाउचर संख्या, आपूर्तिदाता का नाम और वर्तमान स्थान (लोकेशन) दर्ज करना अनिवार्य है।
- कथन IV गलत है: नियम 213(1) के अनुसार सभी अचल परिसंपत्तियों का वर्ष में कम से कम एक बार भौतिक सत्यापन (Physical Verification) अनिवार्य रूप से किया जाना चाहिए ताकि नुकसान, चोरी या अनुपयोगिता की पहचान हो सके।
अतः कथन I, II और III सही हैं, इसलिए विकल्प (A) सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I, II and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Fixed assets including land, buildings, plant, and machinery must be recorded in Form GFR-22, capturing acquisition costs, purchase dates, and physical locations. Contrary to ignoring physical checks, financial rules explicitly mandate periodic physical verification of all fixed assets to ensure structural existence, prevent unauthorized removal, and reconcile physical inventory with account registers.

questions.question_english: A government school possesses 50 broken dual desks that are beyond repair and have been formally condemned by the committee. The assessed scrap value is approximately Rs. 4,000. What is the most practical and rule-compliant method for the Principal to dispose of them under GFR?
options_english: Organize an open advertised national e-auction through central government portals regardless of administrative cost.
Incinerate the broken wooden desks inside the school playground premises to clear storage space immediately.
Sell them to a local scrap vendor by obtaining limited local quotations since the assessed scrap value is minimal.
Distribute the condemned desks free of cost among interested teaching and non-teaching school staff members.
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 218(1)(ii) of GFR 2017, when the assessed residual or scrap value of unserviceable goods is very low (e.g., up to Rs. 2 Lakhs, and particularly in minor amounts like Rs. 4,000), floating open advertised tenders or national e-auctions would incur administrative and advertising costs far exceeding the residual value of the items. The rules therefore permit disposal by inviting limited quotations from local scrap dealers through a transparent, competitive process to realize fair market scrap value. Burning government property creates environmental and fire hazards and is strictly prohibited, while free distribution among staff violates public property stewardship.
questions.explanation_hindi: जीएफआर (GFR), 2017 के नियम 218(1)(ii) के अनुसार, जब अनुपयोगी वस्तुओं का आकलित अवशिष्ट या कबाड़ मूल्य अत्यंत कम (जैसे ₹4,000) होता है, तो राष्ट्रीय स्तर की विज्ञापित निविदा या ई-नीलामी आयोजित करने पर होने वाला प्रशासनिक व्यय प्राप्त होने वाले राजस्व से कहीं अधिक हो जाएगा। अतः वित्तीय नियम ऐसी अल्प-मूल्य वाली वस्तुओं के त्वरित एवं किफायती निपटान हेतु स्थानीय कबाड़ विक्रेताओं से सीमित कोटेशन (limited quotations) आमंत्रित कर पारदर्शी तरीके से बेचने की अनुमति देते हैं। स्कूल परिसर में लकड़ी जलाना पर्यावरण एवं सुरक्षा नियमों के विरुद्ध है तथा स्टाफ में मुफ्त बांटना सरकारी संपत्ति के नियमों का उल्लंघन है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Sell them to a local scrap vendor by obtaining limited local quotations since value is small.

questions.question_english: Which of the following is NOT one of the general principles of financial propriety as codified under Rule 21 of GFR 2017?
options_english: The quantum of allowances granted to meet expenditure should be so regulated that they become an additional source of profit to the recipients.
Every public officer is expected to enforce financial order, strict economy, and fiscal vigilance.
Expenditure from public moneys should not be incurred for the benefit of a particular person or section of people unless specific legal or policy conditions are met.
The expenditure should not be prima facie more than what the occasion legitimately demands.
questions.explanation_english:
Option A is NOT a principle of financial propriety; in fact, the actual rule states exactly the opposite.

Rule 21(iii) of GFR 2017 explicitly mandates:
"The amount of allowances granted to meet expenditure of a particular type should be so regulated that the allowances are not on the whole a source of profit to the recipient."

Official allowances (such as Traveling Allowance, Daily Allowance, or Conveyance Allowance) are designed purely as compensatory reimbursements for out-of-pocket expenses incurred in the performance of public duty. Under no circumstances may they be structured, claimed, or passed to generate personal savings or financial profit for government servants.
questions.explanation_hindi:
विकल्प A वित्तीय औचित्य का सिद्धांत नहीं है; वास्तव में, वास्तविक नियम इसके बिल्कुल विपरीत प्रावधान करता है।

GFR 2017 का नियम 21(iii) स्पष्ट रूप से यह अधिदेश देता है:
"किसी विशेष प्रकार के व्यय को पूरा करने के लिए दिए जाने वाले भत्तों की राशि को इस प्रकार विनियमित किया जाना चाहिए कि वे कुल मिलाकर प्राप्तकर्ता के लिए लाभ का स्रोत न बनें।"

सरकारी भत्ते (जैसे यात्रा भत्ता, दैनिक भत्ता या वाहन भत्ता) पूरी तरह से आधिकारिक कर्तव्यों के निर्वहन में किए गए वास्तविक जेब खर्च की प्रतिपूर्ति (Compensatory Reimbursement) के रूप में दिए जाते हैं। इन्हें किसी भी परिस्थिति में सरकारी कर्मचारियों के लिए व्यक्तिगत लाभ या अतिरिक्त आय का स्रोत नहीं बनाया जा सकता।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) The amount of allowances granted to meet expenditure should be structured to become a source of profit to the recipients.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: expenditure should be structured to become a source of profit to the recipients. Standards of financial propriety stipulate that official allowances granted to public servants are strictly intended to meet legitimate expenses incurred in the discharge of public duties. Allowances must never be structured or manipulated to serve as a source of extra income or personal profit. Every spending authority must maintain financial discipline, avoid unnecessary expenditures, and ensure broad public interest orientation.

questions.question_english: Which fundamental principle of public financial management dictates that no expenditure can be incurred or liability committed by a delegated authority unless there is a specific sanctioned budget provision for it?
options_english: Rule of E-procurement and digital financial processing
Rule on Budgetary Control (No expenditure without budget provision)
Rule of Contingency management and emergency funds allocation
Rule of Advance Payment to commercial contractors and vendors
questions.explanation_english: Under Article 114(3) of the Constitution of India and Rule 52 of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017, no expenditure can be incurred from the Consolidated Fund of India unless it is covered by a specific budget appropriation authorized by Parliament. This cardinal rule of Budgetary Control ('No expenditure without budget') stipulates that no administrative or delegated authority—including school Principals and DDOs—can issue expenditure sanctions, enter into contracts, or make payments in excess of the sanctioned budget grant or without an existing budget allotment under the relevant accounting head. Sanctioning expenditure in anticipation of funds without budget provision violates financial rules and attracts disciplinary liability.
questions.explanation_hindi: भारत के संविधान के अनुच्छेद 114(3) तथा सामान्य वित्तीय नियमावली (GFR) 2017 के नियम 52 के तहत, भारत की संचित निधि से तब तक कोई व्यय नहीं किया जा सकता जब तक कि संसद द्वारा पारित विशिष्ट विनियोग या बजट प्रावधान न हो। बजटीय नियंत्रण का यह मूलभूत सिद्धांत ('बिना बजट प्रावधान के कोई व्यय नहीं') निर्धारित करता है कि कोई भी प्रशासनिक या प्रत्यायोजित प्राधिकारी (जैसे विद्यालय प्राचार्य या DDO) स्वीकृत बजट आवंटन के अभाव में न तो कोई व्यय स्वीकृत कर सकता है, न अनुबंध कर सकता है और न ही भुगतान कर सकता है। बजट प्रावधान के बिना भविष्य में धन मिलने की प्रत्याशा में व्यय स्वीकृत करना वित्तीय नियमों का गंभीर उल्लंघन है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Rule on Budgetary Control (No expenditure without budget)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: without budget) A foundational rule of public financial management dictates that no expenditure can be incurred and no financial liability created unless funds have been formally authorized through specific budget provisions. Budgetary control rules mandate that availability of budget grants is a mandatory prerequisite before any financial sanction or payment commitment is made.
